newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS proposes bigger royalties role for states.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS proposes bigger royalties role for states.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service Wednesday proposed a rule that would allow states to assume more federal royalties management functions.

The MMS, under the direction of the Royalty Simplification and Fairness Act which passed last year, proposed a rule that would allow states to get authority for receiving and processing production and royalty reports, correcting erroneous report data, and verifying automated data.
States also could get authority for issuing demands, oil and gas subpoenas, orders to perform restructured accounting, and related tolling agreements and notices to lessees.
"MMS is also proposing the delegation of many of these functions associated with solid mineral, geothermal and certain offshore leases," MMS Director Cynthia Quarterman said in a statement.
"We believe that it is most efficient to delegate functions for these other leases since they comprise a significant amount of activity in several states," she said.
MMS, which is to set the standards by August 13, said it will accept comments for 30 days.
